questions.q: Why does Oracle keep Transfer Journal Entries to GL as a separate step from Create Accounting's Final mode?
options: Because Final mode cannot actually create any journal entries
To give a controller a clean checkpoint, letting final subledger accounting accumulate and be spot-checked before a deliberate transfer to GL
Because General Ledger does not support journal batches
There is no real reason; it is purely an accident of system design
questions.explain: Separating creation from transfer provides a deliberate checkpoint rather than pushing every transaction into GL continuously.

questions.q: What does the Transfer Journal Entries to GL process actually do?
options: It deletes Draft subledger journal entries
It moves eligible Final subledger journal entries into General Ledger as GL journal batches
It creates new accounting events in a subledger application
It validates an Application Accounting Definition
questions.explain: The process takes Final, not-yet-transferred subledger journal entries and moves them into General Ledger as journal batches.

questions.q: What is the effect of selecting the "Post in General Ledger" option during transfer?
options: It prevents the journal from ever reaching General Ledger
It also posts the journal as part of the same run, updating account balances immediately, instead of arriving as an unposted batch
It deletes the original subledger journal entry
It automatically reverses the entry
questions.explain: When selected, the transferred journal is also posted immediately; when not selected, it arrives unposted for separate posting later.

questions.q: Which subledger journal entries are eligible to be picked up by Transfer Journal Entries to GL?
options: Only Draft entries
Both Draft and Final entries equally
Only Final entries that have not already been transferred in a previous run
Entries from any status, as long as they are less than a year old
questions.explain: Draft entries can never be transferred; only Final, not-yet-transferred entries qualify for a transfer run.

questions.q: What happens to a subledger journal entry that is new in Final status but was somehow missed by a previous transfer run?
options: It is permanently lost and can never be transferred
It remains eligible and will be picked up as an eligible leftover entry by a later transfer run
It must be manually re-entered as a brand-new transaction
It automatically converts back to Draft status
questions.explain: Transfer Journal Entries to GL can pick up eligible leftover entries from previous runs that were not yet transferred, in addition to the current run's entries.
